## Problem 1
```{r}
shared_birthday = function(n) {

  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)

  any(duplicated(birthdays))

}

birthday_results =
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    shared = map_lgl(group_size, shared_birthday)
  )

birthday_summary =
  birthday_results |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(
    probability = mean(shared),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r, birthday_plot}
birthday_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 1.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of at least one shared birthday",
    x = "Number of people",
    y = "Estimated probability"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

```{r, shared_birthday_examples, include=FALSE}
birthday_summary |>
  filter(group_size %in% c(2, 25, 50))
```

Across 10,000 simulations per group size, the estimated probability of at ≥1 shared birthday increased with bigger group size. For example, the probability was 0.28% with 2 people, 57.5% with 25 people, and 96.8% with 50 people. This occurs because larger groups contain more pairs of people who could share a birthday.
